items.hook: The peerage and clergy restrict the authority of English kings with the Ordinances of 1311.
items.body: England is a country that is part of the United Kingdom. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Soyuz MS-10, launching an intended crew for the ISS, suffers an in-flight abort. The crew lands safely.
items.body: Soyuz MS-10 was a crewed Soyuz MS spaceflight that aborted shortly after launch on 11 October 2018 due to a failure of the Soyuz-FG launch vehicle boosters. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Nearly 1 in 10 young adults could have fatty, narrow arteries
items.body: Atherosclerosis, the build-up of fatty plaque in arteries, usually affects people older than 50, but a "meaningful" proportion of younger adults also have the condition

items.body: Northern Irish composer Hannah Peel picked up the discovery of the year award.

items.hook: The Royal Navy decisively defeats the Batavian Navy at Camperdown during the French Revolutionary Wars.
items.body: The Battle of Camperdown was fought on 11 October 1797 between the Royal Navy's North Sea Fleet under Admiral of the Blue Adam Duncan and a Batavian Navy fleet led by Vice-admiral Jan Willem de Winter. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Li Yaotang, better known by his pen name Ba Jin or his courtesy name Li Feigan, was a Chinese anarchist, translator, and writer.
items.body: In addition to his impact on Chinese literature, he also wrote three original works in Esperanto, and as a political activist he wrote The Family. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: William Francis Ross "Frank" Hardie was a Scottish classicist, philosopher and academic.
items.body: He was President of Corpus Christi College, Oxford, from 1950 to 1969. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Depression Quest is a 2013 interactive fiction game dealing with the subject of depression.
items.body: It was developed by Zoë Quinn using the Twine engine, with writing by Quinn and Patrick Lindsey, and music by Isaac Schankler. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: The First Lady of Jazz is a statue of Ella Fitzgerald situated outside the Yonkers Metro-North station in the city of Yonkers in Westchester County, New York, United States.
items.body: It was unveiled in October 1996; Fitzgerald had died in June 1996 at the age of 79. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Caliph al-Muttaqi is blinded and deposed by the Turkish general Tuzun.
items.body: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Jaʿfar al-Muqtadir better known by his regnal title al-Muttaqi was the Abbasid Caliph in Baghdad from 940 to 944. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: The Royal Indian Engineering College was a British college of Civil Engineering run by the India Office to train civil engineers for service in the Indian Public Works Department.
items.body: It was located on the Cooper's Hill estate, near Egham, Surrey. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: George Washington is posthumously promoted to the grade of General of the Armies.
items.body: George Washington was a Founding Father and the first president of the United States, serving from 1789 to 1797. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Prof. Anita Hill delivers her televised testimony concerning sexual harassment during the Clarence Thomas Supreme Court nomination.
